recognize_zh: 箭頭所指的紅血球比周圍紅血球略大、顏色較淡，內含一個細胞質環、只有單一紅色染色質點的環狀體（ring form），而且整個視野只見單一感染，符合間日瘧（P. vivax）偏好感染網狀紅血球的特徵。
features: Single infected red cell slightly larger and paler than adjacent erythrocytes
Intraerythrocytic ring form with thin blue cytoplasmic ring and a single red-purple chromatin dot
Low parasitemia: no multiply infected cells, no appliqué forms, no gametocytes in this field
Background erythrocytes are normocytic; scattered platelets and smear artifacts (fiber, scratches)
describe_en: Thin peripheral blood smear shows a single intraerythrocytic ring-form parasite with a delicate cytoplasmic ring and one chromatin dot. The infected erythrocyte is slightly enlarged and paler than the surrounding red cells, suggesting infection of a reticulocyte. There are no multiply infected erythrocytes, appliqué forms, or banana-shaped gametocytes in this field, and parasitemia appears low. Findings are suggestive of Plasmodium vivax ring form; species confirmation should include review of later-stage forms (amoeboid trophozoites, Schüffner stippling) and/or PCR.

ddx.vs: P. falciparum rings are small and delicate in normal-sized red cells, often with double chromatin dots, appliqué forms and multiple rings per cell, with high parasitemia.
P. ovale also infects enlarged reticulocytes but the host cells are often oval with fimbriated edges and Schüffner dots.
Babesia forms are pleomorphic small rings without pigment that may form extracellular clusters and tetrad 'Maltese cross' forms.
An overlying platelet shows a halo and granular purple material without a true cytoplasmic ring and chromatin dot in the same focal plane.
